stories.delivered_paragraph: Spotify added 1 million more Premium subscribers than it expected in the second quarter, helping it meet its revenue-growth target despite a slight miss in monthly-user growth. Revenue rose 14%, while gross margin expanded by 193 basis points to 33.4% and operating income reached €655 million. Co-CEOs Alex Norström and Gustav Söderström said AI playlisting and remix tools have strong momentum, while emphasizing that AI and marketing spending remain under the company’s control.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Lenovo has cut the price of its Legion Go S SteamOS handheld to $635.54 with checkout code EXTRASAVEAFF, down from a listed $1,137.41 and its lowest recorded price. The Z2 Go-powered model has an 8-inch, 120Hz variable-refresh-rate IPS screen and is positioned as a SteamOS alternative to the Steam Deck OLED. Performance is broadly comparable to the pricier OLED Steam Deck, making the deal most appealing to players willing to lower settings in demanding games.

stories.delivered_paragraph: OpenAI agreed to pay $3.2 million to settle Justice Department allegations that it discriminated against U.S. workers by favoring temporary visa holders in hiring. The company said it disagrees with the DOJ’s findings but settled the case, while the department said OpenAI would redress harm and change its recruiting practices. The agreement puts a prominent AI company at the center of the Trump administration’s broader scrutiny of employers’ use of visa programs for high-demand technology jobs.

stories.delivered_paragraph: BMW is displaying Spider-Man: Brand New Day banner ads on some drivers’ dashboard control screens when they start their cars, under a promotional partnership with Marvel. The campaign runs from July 27 through August 10 in more than 70 countries on eligible vehicles built after July 2020 and using several versions of BMW’s operating system. Tapping the ad opens an animated promotion featuring the iX3, extending movie marketing into a car interface that owners may not expect to contain advertising.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Senate Democrats say major banks failed to report suspicious transfers involving Jeffrey Epstein until after his 2019 arrest, according to a new committee report. stories.delivered_paragraph: French rescuers brought 173 migrants ashore at Boulogne-sur-Mer after the engine of their small boat caught fire during an attempted Channel crossing to Britain. Eleven people suffered minor injuries, French prosecutors opened an investigation, and an Egyptian national was taken into custody in connection with the incident. The rescue underscores the continuing danger of the crossings, even as the UK government says those rescued will be returned to France and officials target the smuggling networks involved.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Leonardo DiCaprio’s Re:wild and the Bezos Earth Fund have launched the $200 million Phoenix Species Project to help recover 100 species facing imminent extinction. The initiative will support mammals, amphibians, reptiles, birds, fish, invertebrates and plants across 30 countries, from ocean habitats to volcanic plains. By concentrating funds on species judged close to disappearing, the project aims to turn celebrity-backed conservation financing into measurable recovery work rather than broad awareness alone.

stories.delivered_paragraph: The Writers Guild of America will hold its 79th annual awards ceremonies on February 13, 2027, at the Edison Ballroom in New York and the Fairmont Century Plaza in Los Angeles. stories.delivered_paragraph: The Killers frontman Brandon Flowers, 45, says he is questioning how much longer he wants to pursue life as a rock star as he prepares to release his third solo album, Thrasher, on August 21. stories.delivered_paragraph: Science communicator Hank Green is stepping back from production after criticism of his AI use, which he called “not healthy,” although he says he used chatbots to find research sources rather than write scripts. The debate has focused on the tension between a creator’s credibility and a technology prone to plausible-sounding errors and trained on often uncompensated work. stories.delivered_paragraph: Brent crude fell almost 5% to below $80 a barrel, a three-week low, after senior U.S. officials said talks with Iran might allow shipping through the Strait of Hormuz to resume as soon as this week. U.S. West Texas Intermediate dropped more than 5% to $76, as traders priced in the possibility of eased supply disruption. The decline could relieve pressure on fuel prices, but officials said no final agreement had been reached and previous talks have failed to stabilize the market.

stories.delivered_paragraph: Palantir shares surged as much as 30% after the company reported second-quarter revenue of $1.94 billion, up 93% from a year earlier and above the $1.8 billion analysts expected. Commercial revenue jumped 149% to $764 million and government revenue rose 90% to $809 million, driven by demand for tools that let customers use AI while retaining control of their data. The results and higher full-year outlook signal that AI spending is translating into unusually rapid growth for a large enterprise-software company.

stories.delivered_paragraph: America’s richest 20% of households are buying most new cars sold in the United States, according to MarketWatch, as an AI-fueled stock-market rally boosts wealth at the top. The pattern suggests carmakers are increasingly dependent on affluent consumers even as many households face high vehicle prices and borrowing costs. That concentration can support sales of expensive models in the near term, but it also leaves the market more exposed if asset prices or high-income spending weaken.
